page: Microsoft Azure D8lds_v5 is a compute-oriented virtual machine configuration within the general purpose and compute-focused Azure portfolio. Built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance provides 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at a base frequency of 2.8 GHz. The architecture incorporates 48 KB L1 data cache per core, 1 MB L2 cache per core, and a shared 48 MB L3 cache, backed by vector extensions such as AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512 VNNI alongside hardware cryptographic acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

The configuration provides 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 2.0 GB per vCPU allocation ratio typical of compute-leaning tiers. Bundled with the instance is 322 GB of local SSD storage, providing high-speed scratch space directly on the host hypervisor. In memory benchmarks, the platform demonstrates sustained throughput of 58.77 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 41.56 GB/sec for large-block uncached writes, accompanied by 419.63 GB/sec in small-block cached read operations.

Benchmark results position the D8lds_v5 within average mid-tier ranges across standard compute and operational workloads. The CPU achieves a PassMark score of 11,429.18, a Geekbench single-core score of 1,595.0, and a multi-core score of 6,034.0. Application-level evaluations record 7.97 million Redis SET operations per second and 11.32 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. A performance tradeoff appears in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, which falls into the lower 25th percentile at 31.24 GB/sec despite solid single-core compression metrics.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D8lds_v5 optimizes compute density by pairing 8 vCPUs with a lean 16 GB memory footprint and integrated local SSD capacity. This profile reduces per-core platform costs compared to standard 4:1 memory configurations while avoiding external storage costs for transient files. The server fits batch computing, code compilation, CI/CD build agents, web serving tiers, and intermediate ETL workers that demand consistent CPU cycles without high RAM overhead.
description: Microsoft Azure D8lds_v5 is an 8-vCPU virtual machine built on a dedicated 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon 8370C processor with 4 physical cores and simultaneous multithreading. It features 16.0 GB of RAM, establishing a compute-oriented 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio, and includes a 322 GB local SSD for high-throughput temporary storage. The processor incorporates AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, VAES, and SHA-NI acceleration. Benchmark evaluations place the instance solidly in the median tier, returning a Geekbench multi-core score of 6,034.0, a PassMark CPU score of 11,429.18, and 7.97 million Redis SET operations per second. Multi-threaded decompression exhibits lower relative efficiency, but the instance maintains balanced single-thread compute and static web throughput of 11.32 GB/sec. The D8lds_v5 is well suited for CPU-focused workloads, web serving, software build pipelines, and processing tasks with modest memory footprints.
